record.title: VideoXAgent reports competitive long-video results with query-driven expert tools
record.summary: A September 11 preprint introduces VideoXAgent, an online harness that decomposes a video question and invokes specialized tools such as detection, OCR, speech recognition and frame inspection as needed. The authors report competitive performance on Video-MME-Long, LongVideoBench-Long, LVBench and MINERVA; on MINERVA they report 65.7% accuracy and about 15% of the context footprint of a 1,024-frame dense-packing baseline. The paper says its efficiency measure counts retrieved evidence and maximum agent context, not total token cost. These are author-reported benchmark results; the review did not run the system or independently reproduce them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: VideoXAgent is an online harness that decomposes long-video questions and invokes specialized tools to gather multimodal evidence as needed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 85.1% on Video-MME-Long, 76.5% on LVBench and 65.7% on MINERVA with about 50k agent-context tokens per sample; on MINERVA they report performance in the range of frontier systems at about 15% of a 1,024-frame dense-packing baseline context footprint.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: These results do not establish lower total token or compute cost, independent reproduction, or performance outside the reported benchmark and evaluation regime.

evidence_gaps.description: Reported benchmark and context-footprint results have not been independently reproduced.
The paper’s efficiency metric omits total token cost and does not provide a full lifecycle comparison across tool calls and models.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported benchmark results hold, an online video agent that selectively acquires evidence could reduce context use in long-video analysis, a relevant systems design for multimodal agents. The result is notable rather than field-shifting because the evidence is author-reported on four benchmarks, the context metric excludes total token cost, and no independent reproduction was inspected.
limitations: All benchmark results are author-reported; the research desk did not run the code or independently reproduce the measurements.
The paper defines efficiency through retrieved evidence and maximum agent-model context, not total token cost; total compute economics are not established.
The capability taxonomy is mined from MINERVA expert reasoning traces and may reflect dataset-specific distributions.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report competitive results on four long-video benchmarks and a smaller measured context footprint on MINERVA using query-driven specialized tools.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper measures retrieved evidence and maximum agent context, not total token cost. It does not establish end-to-end compute, latency, or monetary savings.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper reports benchmark measurements. No code was run and no independent reproduction was performed in this activation; the results remain CLAIMED.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint describing an online video agent and specialized tools. This review did not verify a pinned code/model artifact or run the system.
technical.mechanism: Given a video and question, the agent decomposes the task, invokes perception tools as evidence is needed, and aggregates their observations into an answer. Tools include scripts, vision-language models, and specialists for detection, OCR, speech recognition, and temporal localization.
technical.novelty: The work derives an atomic capability taxonomy from expert reasoning traces and maps it to heterogeneous tools. The agent acquires evidence online for each query rather than requiring a prebuilt full-video representation.
technical.regime: The article evaluates Video-MME-Long, LongVideoBench-Long, LVBench, and MINERVA. Its efficiency comparisons use retrieved evidence and maximum agent context. The capability taxonomy is mined from MINERVA traces.
technical.reproducibility: This review inspected arXiv HTML v1 but did not pin or run code/models or independently reproduce the results. Measurements are reported by the authors.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares with prior multimodal models and video agents on the evaluated benchmarks. Its MINERVA context comparison uses a 1,024-frame dense-packing baseline; context footprint is not total compute or token cost.

brief.title: VideoXAgent reports competitive long-video results with query-driven expert tools
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported results generalize, query-conditioned tool use could reduce the context needed to answer questions about long videos while retaining benchmark performance. The paper makes a useful design case for progressive evidence acquisition, but its comparison does not establish lower total compute cost, generality beyond the evaluated datasets, or independently replicated performance.
